title: “Kriya Yoga: Portal to the Infinite” by Brother Anandamoy
formattedMarkdown:
# Kriya Yoga: Portal to the Infinite

### Opening Reflections

My dear friends, we gather here to discuss the most profound gift bestowed upon us by our Paramguru, Swami Sri Yukteswar, and brought to the West by our beloved Paramahansa Yogananda: the scientific technique of Kriya Yoga. It is not merely a practice; it is a portal to the Infinite, a path to liberate the soul from the clutches of ego-delusion.

### The Nature of Kriya Yoga

Kriya Yoga is not a path of belief. It is a path of direct experience. As Yogananda used to say, 'Self-realization is the knowing in all parts of body, mind, and soul that you are now in possession of the kingdom of God.' Kriya Yoga accelerates this process by neutralizing the currents of the life force that keep our consciousness tethered to the external world.

**Story • The Master and the Restless Mind**

Story: I recall a time in the early days when a young student came to Yogananda complaining that his meditation was nothing but a 'circus of thoughts.' He was frustrated. Master smiled, with that twinkle in his eyes that could pierce through any gloom, and said, 'My child, you are trying to catch a bird with your bare hands while standing in a windstorm. Kriya is not catching the bird; it is calming the wind.' The student practiced the technique, not as a duty, but as a love offering to the Divine, and within weeks, the stillness he sought began to bloom from within.

### The Mechanics of Liberation

Why does Kriya work? Because we are essentially energy beings. The spine is the altar of the soul. By consciously directing the life force (prana) up and down the spine, we transmute the heavy, physical vibration of the senses into the subtle vibration of the spirit. We are, in essence, rewiring our nervous system to handle the high voltage of divine consciousness.

### The Necessity of Dispassion

We must understand that as long as we identify with the body, we will suffer. Kriya Yoga helps us detach. It is like a ladder. If you want to reach the roof, you must leave the ground. You cannot hold onto the comfort of your attachments and expect to soar into the Infinite.

**Story • The Fisherman and the Golden Net**

Story: There was once a fisherman who spent his life casting a net, hoping to catch a single fish of gold. He labored for years, dragging the heavy net through the mud. One day, a sage walked by and asked, 'Why do you labor so hard for a metal that will only weigh you down?' The fisherman realized he had been catching only the burdens of the world. The sage taught him that the net was meant to gather light, not heavy earth. Kriya Yoga is that golden net. It pulls the consciousness out of the muddy waters of the senses and into the clear, luminous light of the spiritual eye.

### Conclusion: The Path Ahead

Do not be discouraged by the length of the journey. One step at a time, one Kriya at a time. The Infinite is not far away; it is closer than your own breath. When you practice, do so with yearning—a deep, unquenchable thirst for the Divine. That is the key that opens the portal.

May you find that stillness, that peace that passes all understanding.
